items.text: I can explain what an Auto Scaling Group (ASG) is and the problem it solves
I know the three things ASG needs: Launch Template, Size Limits, and Scaling Policy
I understand Minimum Size, Desired Capacity, and Maximum Size and how they interact
I can name all 4 scaling policy types: Manual, Dynamic, Predictive, Scheduled
I understand the 3 sub-types of Dynamic Scaling: Step, Simple, and Target Tracking
I can explain what a Load Balancer does and why it's needed with multiple EC2 instances
I know the 4 types of AWS load balancers and which layer each operates at
I understand ALB components: Listener, Rules, and Target Groups and how they connect
I can explain path-based routing and host-based routing with real examples
I understand ELB health checks vs EC2 health checks and why ELB checks matter
I can create a Launch Template with AMI, instance type, security group, and user data
I can create a Target Group and configure HTTP health checks
I can create an Application Load Balancer with listeners and routing rules
I can create an ASG, set size limits, attach it to an ALB Target Group, and configure Target Tracking
I can verify ASG instances are InService and Target Group shows all Healthy
I know how to clean up ASG, ALB, Target Group, and Launch Template to avoid charges
I can answer: 'When should you use Target Tracking vs Scheduled vs Predictive Scaling?'
I can answer: 'What is the difference between ALB and NLB? When to use each?'
I can answer: 'How does ASG ensure high availability when an EC2 instance fails?'
I can answer: 'What makes vertical scaling risky compared to horizontal scaling?'
I can identify Single Point of Failure scenarios and explain how ASG+ALB eliminates them
